audit_status.source_base: Hebrew Judges / Shoftim Samson birth-annunciation and Manoah household narrative, draft aligned later
audit_status.review_note: First-pass draft reviewed for unnamed woman's primary revelation, infertility language, prenatal Nazirite instructions, Manoah's repeated inquiry, messenger/name language, wondrous altar scene, the wife's theological reasoning, Samson naming, blessing, and Spirit stirring.

verses.restored: Children of Israel again did evil in eyes of YHWH, and YHWH gave them into hand of Philistines forty years.

familiar.text: And the children of Israel did evil again in the sight of the LORD; and the LORD delivered them into the hand of the Philistines forty years.

modern.text: Again the Israelites did evil in the sight of the LORD, so He delivered them into the hand of the Philistines for forty years.

original.text: וַיֹּסִ֨פוּ֙ בְּנֵ֣י יִשְׂרָאֵ֔ל לַעֲשׂ֥וֹת הָרַ֖ע בְּעֵינֵ֣י יְהוָ֑ה וַיִּתְּנֵ֧ם יְהוָ֛ה בְּיַד פְּלִשְׁתִּ֖ים אַרְבָּעִ֥ים שָׁנָֽה

verses.restored: There was one man from Zorah, from clan of Danite, and his name was Manoah. His wife had not borne children.

familiar.text: And there was a certain man of Zorah, of the family of the Danites, whose name was Manoah; and his wife was barren, and bare not.

modern.text: Now there was a man from Zorah named Manoah, from the clan of the Danites, whose wife was barren and had no children.

original.text: וַיְהִי֩ אִ֨ישׁ אֶחָ֧ד מִצָּרְעָ֛ה מִמִּשְׁפַּ֥חַת הַדָּנִ֖י וּשְׁמ֣וֹ מָנ֑וֹחַ וְאִשְׁתּ֥וֹ עֲקָרָ֖ה וְלֹ֥א יָלָֽדָה

verses.restored: Messenger of YHWH appeared to the woman and said to her, Look, please: you have not borne, but you shall conceive and bear a son.

familiar.text: And the angel of the LORD appeared unto the woman, and said unto her, Behold now, thou art barren, and bearest not: but thou shalt conceive, and bear a son.

modern.text: The angel of the LORD appeared to the woman and said to her, “It is true that you are barren and have no children; but you will conceive and give birth to a son.

original.text: וַיֵּרָ֥א מַלְאַךְ יְהוָ֖ה אֶל הָאִשָּׁ֑ה וַיֹּ֣אמֶר אֵלֶ֗יהָ הִנֵּה נָ֤א אַתְּ עֲקָרָה֙ וְלֹ֣א יָלַ֔דְתְּ וְהָרִ֖ית וְיָלַ֥דְתְּ בֵּֽן

verses.restored: Now guard yourself, please: do not drink wine or strong drink, and do not eat anything unclean.

familiar.text: Now therefore beware, I pray thee, and drink not wine nor strong drink, and eat not any unclean thing:

modern.text: Now please be careful not to drink wine or strong drink, and not to eat anything unclean.

original.text: וְעַתָּה֙ הִשָּׁ֣מְרִי נָ֔א וְאַל תִּשְׁתִּ֖י יַ֣יִן וְשֵׁכָ֑ר וְאַל תֹּאכְלִ֖י כָּל טָמֵֽא

verses.restored: For look, you shall conceive and bear a son, and a razor shall not go up over his head, because the boy shall be a Nazirite of Divine from womb; he shall begin to save Israel from hand of Philistines.

familiar.text: For, lo, thou shalt conceive, and bear a son; and no razor shall come on his head: for the child shall be a Nazarite unto God from the womb: and he shall begin to deliver Israel out of the hand of the Philistines.

modern.text: For behold, you will conceive and give birth to a son. And no razor shall come over his head, because the boy will be a Nazirite to God from the womb, and he will begin the deliverance of Israel from the hand of the Philistines.”

original.text: כִּי֩ הִנָּ֨ךְ הָרָ֜ה וְיֹלַ֣דְתְּ בֵּ֗ן וּמוֹרָה֙ לֹא יַעֲלֶ֣ה עַל רֹאשׁ֔וֹ כִּֽי נְזִ֧יר אֱלֹהִ֛ים יִהְיֶ֥ה הַנַּ֖עַר מִן הַבָּ֑טֶן וְה֗וּא יָחֵ֛ל לְהוֹשִׁ֥יעַ אֶת יִשְׂרָאֵ֖ל מִיַּ֥ד פְּלִשְׁתִּֽים

verses.restored: The woman came and said to her husband, saying, A man of Divine came to me, and his appearance was like appearance of a messenger of Divine, very awe-inspiring. I did not ask him where he was from, and he did not tell me his name.

familiar.text: Then the woman came and told her husband, saying, A man of God came unto me, and his countenance was like the countenance of an angel of God, very terrible: but I asked him not whence he was, neither told he me his name:

modern.text: So the woman went and told her husband, “A man of God came to me. His appearance was like the angel of God, exceedingly awesome. I did not ask him where he came from, and he did not tell me his name.

original.text: וַתָּבֹ֣א הָאִשָּׁ֗ה וַתֹּ֣אמֶר לְאִישָׁהּ֮ לֵאמֹר֒ אִ֤ישׁ הָאֱלֹהִים֙ בָּ֣א אֵלַ֔י וּמַרְאֵ֕הוּ כְּמַרְאֵ֛ה מַלְאַ֥ךְ הָאֱלֹהִ֖ים נוֹרָ֣א מְאֹ֑ד וְלֹ֤א שְׁאִלְתִּ֨יהוּ֙ אֵֽי מִזֶּ֣ה ה֔וּא וְאֶת שְׁמ֖וֹ לֹֽא הִגִּ֥יד לִֽי

verses.restored: He said to me, Look, you shall conceive and bear a son. Now do not drink wine or strong drink, and do not eat any unclean thing, because the boy shall be a Nazirite of Divine from womb until day of his death.

familiar.text: But he said unto me, Behold, thou shalt conceive, and bear a son; and now drink no wine nor strong drink, neither eat any unclean thing: for the child shall be a Nazarite to God from the womb to the day of his death.

modern.text: But he said to me, ‘Behold, you will conceive and give birth to a son. Now, therefore, do not drink wine or strong drink, and do not eat anything unclean, because the boy will be a Nazirite to God from the womb until the day of his death.’”

original.text: וַיֹּ֣אמֶר לִ֔י הִנָּ֥ךְ הָרָ֖ה וְיֹלַ֣דְתְּ בֵּ֑ן וְעַתָּ֞ה אַל תִּשְׁתִּ֣י יַ֣יִן וְשֵׁכָ֗ר וְאַל תֹּֽאכְלִי֙ כָּל טֻמְאָ֔ה כִּֽי נְזִ֤יר אֱלֹהִים֙ יִהְיֶ֣ה הַנַּ֔עַר מִן הַבֶּ֖טֶן עַד י֥וֹם מוֹתֽוֹ

verses.restored: Manoah pleaded with YHWH and said, Please, my Lord, let the man of Divine whom you sent come again to us and teach us what we shall do for the boy who will be born.

familiar.text: Then Manoah intreated the LORD, and said, O my Lord, let the man of God which thou didst send come again unto us, and teach us what we shall do unto the child that shall be born.

modern.text: Then Manoah prayed to the LORD, “Please, O Lord, let the man of God You sent us come to us again to teach us how to raise the boy who is to be born.”

original.text: וַיֶּעְתַּ֥ר מָנ֛וֹחַ אֶל יְהוָ֖ה וַיֹּאמַ֑ר בִּ֣י אֲדוֹנָ֔י אִ֣ישׁ הָאֱלֹהִ֞ים אֲשֶׁ֣ר שָׁלַ֗חְתָּ יָבוֹא נָ֥א עוֹד֙ אֵלֵ֔ינוּ וְיוֹרֵ֕נוּ מַֽה נַּעֲשֶׂ֖ה לַנַּ֥עַר הַיּוּלָּֽד

verses.restored: Divine listened to voice of Manoah, and messenger of Divine came again to the woman while she was sitting in field; Manoah her husband was not with her.

familiar.text: And God hearkened to the voice of Manoah; and the angel of God came again unto the woman as she sat in the field: but Manoah her husband was not with her.

modern.text: And God listened to the voice of Manoah, and the angel of God returned to the woman as she was sitting in the field; but her husband Manoah was not with her.

original.text: וַיִּשְׁמַ֥ע הָאֱלֹהִ֖ים בְּק֣וֹל מָנ֑וֹחַ וַיָּבֹ֣א מַלְאַךְ֩ הָאֱלֹהִ֨ים ע֜וֹד אֶל הָאִשָּׁ֗ה וְהִיא֙ יוֹשֶׁ֣בֶת בַּשָּׂדֶ֔ה וּמָנ֥וֹחַ אִישָׁ֖הּ אֵ֥ין עִמָּֽהּ

verses.restored: The woman hurried and ran and told her husband. She said to him, Look, the man who came to me that day has appeared to me.

familiar.text: And the woman made haste, and ran, and shewed her husband, and said unto him, Behold, the man hath appeared unto me, that came unto me the other day.

modern.text: The woman ran quickly to tell her husband, “Behold, the man who came to me the other day has reappeared!”

original.text: וַתְּמַהֵר֙ הָֽאִשָּׁ֔ה וַתָּ֖רָץ וַתַּגֵּ֣ד לְאִישָׁ֑הּ וַתֹּ֣אמֶר אֵלָ֔יו הִנֵּ֨ה נִרְאָ֤ה אֵלַי֙ הָאִ֔ישׁ אֲשֶׁר בָּ֥א בַיּ֖וֹם אֵלָֽי

verses.restored: Manoah rose and went after his wife. He came to the man and said to him, Are you the man who spoke to the woman? He said, I am.

familiar.text: And Manoah arose, and went after his wife, and came to the man, and said unto him, Art thou the man that spakest unto the woman? And he said, I am.

modern.text: So Manoah got up and followed his wife. When he came to the man, he asked, “Are you the man who spoke to my wife?” “I am,” he said.

original.text: וַיָּ֛קָם וַיֵּ֥לֶךְ מָנ֖וֹחַ אַחֲרֵ֣י אִשְׁתּ֑וֹ וַיָּבֹא֙ אֶל הָאִ֔ישׁ וַיֹּ֣אמֶר ל֗וֹ הַאַתָּ֥ה הָאִ֛ישׁ אֲשֶׁר דִּבַּ֥רְתָּ אֶל הָאִשָּׁ֖ה וַיֹּ֥אמֶר אָֽנִי

verses.restored: Manoah said, Now let your words come: what shall be rule/way of the boy, and his work?

familiar.text: And Manoah said, Now let thy words come to pass. How shall we order the child, and how shall we do unto him?

modern.text: Then Manoah asked, “When your words come to pass, what will be the boy’s rule of life and mission?”

original.text: וַיֹּ֣אמֶר מָנ֔וֹחַ עַתָּ֖ה יָבֹ֣א דְבָרֶ֑יךָ מַה יִּֽהְיֶ֥ה מִשְׁפַּט הַנַּ֖עַר וּמַעֲשֵֽׂהוּ

verses.restored: Messenger of YHWH said to Manoah, From all that I said to the woman, she shall guard herself.

familiar.text: And the angel of the LORD said unto Manoah, Of all that I said unto the woman let her beware.

modern.text: So the angel of the LORD answered Manoah, “Your wife is to do everything I told her.

original.text: וַיֹּ֛אמֶר מַלְאַ֥ךְ יְהוָ֖ה אֶל מָנ֑וֹחַ מִכֹּ֛ל אֲשֶׁר אָמַ֥רְתִּי אֶל הָאִשָּׁ֖ה תִּשָּׁמֵֽר

verses.restored: She shall not eat from anything that comes from vine of wine; wine and strong drink she shall not drink, and any unclean thing she shall not eat. All that I commanded her, she shall keep.

familiar.text: She may not eat of any thing that cometh of the vine, neither let her drink wine or strong drink, nor eat any unclean thing: all that I commanded her let her observe.

modern.text: She must not eat anything that comes from the vine, nor drink any wine or strong drink, nor eat anything unclean. She must do everything I have commanded her.”

original.text: מִכֹּ֣ל אֲשֶׁר יֵצֵא֩ מִגֶּ֨פֶן הַיַּ֜יִן לֹ֣א תֹאכַ֗ל וְיַ֤יִן וְשֵׁכָר֙ אַל תֵּ֔שְׁתְּ וְכָל טֻמְאָ֖ה אַל תֹּאכַ֑ל כֹּ֥ל אֲשֶׁר צִוִּיתִ֖יהָ תִּשְׁמֹֽר

verses.restored: Manoah said to messenger of YHWH, Please let us detain you, and let us prepare before you a young goat.

familiar.text: And Manoah said unto the angel of the LORD, I pray thee, let us detain thee, until we shall have made ready a kid for thee.

modern.text: “Please stay here,” Manoah said to the angel of the LORD, “and we will prepare a young goat for you.”

original.text: וַיֹּ֥אמֶר מָנ֖וֹחַ אֶל מַלְאַ֣ךְ יְהוָ֑ה נַעְצְרָה נָּ֣א אוֹתָ֔ךְ וְנַעֲשֶׂ֥ה לְפָנֶ֖יךָ גְּדִ֥י עִזִּֽים

verses.restored: Messenger of YHWH said to Manoah, If you detain me, I will not eat from your bread; and if you prepare an ascending offering, to YHWH you shall bring it up. Manoah did not know that he was messenger of YHWH.

familiar.text: And the angel of the LORD said unto Manoah, Though thou detain me, I will not eat of thy bread: and if thou wilt offer a burnt offering, thou must offer it unto the LORD. For Manoah knew not that he was an angel of the LORD.

modern.text: And the angel of the LORD replied, “Even if I stay, I will not eat your food. But if you prepare a burnt offering, offer it to the LORD.” For Manoah did not know that it was the angel of the LORD.

original.text: וַיֹּאמֶר֩ מַלְאַ֨ךְ יְהוָ֜ה אֶל מָנ֗וֹחַ אִם תַּעְצְרֵ֨נִי֙ לֹא אֹכַ֣ל בְּלַחְמֶ֔ךָ וְאִם תַּעֲשֶׂ֣ה עֹלָ֔ה לַיהוָ֖ה תַּעֲלֶ֑נָּה כִּ֚י לֹא יָדַ֣ע מָנ֔וֹחַ כִּֽי מַלְאַ֥ךְ יְהוָ֖ה הֽוּא

verses.restored: Manoah said to messenger of YHWH, What is your name, so that when your word comes we may honor you?

familiar.text: And Manoah said unto the angel of the LORD, What is thy name, that when thy sayings come to pass we may do thee honour?

modern.text: Then Manoah said to the angel of the LORD, “What is your name, so that we may honor you when your word comes to pass?”

original.text: וַיֹּ֧אמֶר מָנ֛וֹחַ אֶל מַלְאַ֥ךְ יְהוָ֖ה מִ֣י שְׁמֶ֑ךָ כִּֽי יָבֹ֥א דבריך וְכִבַּדְנֽוּךָ

verses.restored: Messenger of YHWH said to him, Why do you ask this for my name, when it is wondrous/beyond understanding?

familiar.text: And the angel of the LORD said unto him, Why askest thou thus after my name, seeing it is secret?

modern.text: “Why do you ask my name,” said the angel of the LORD, “since it is beyond comprehension?”

original.text: וַיֹּ֤אמֶר לּוֹ֙ מַלְאַ֣ךְ יְהוָ֔ה לָ֥מָּה זֶּ֖ה תִּשְׁאַ֣ל לִשְׁמִ֑י וְהוּא פֶ֛לִאי

verses.restored: Manoah took young goat and grain offering and brought them up on the rock to YHWH; the one was doing wondrously, while Manoah and his wife were watching.

familiar.text: So Manoah took a kid with a meat offering, and offered it upon a rock unto the LORD: and the angel did wonderously; and Manoah and his wife looked on.

modern.text: Then Manoah took a young goat and a grain offering and offered them on a rock to the LORD. And as Manoah and his wife looked on, the LORD did a marvelous thing.

original.text: וַיִּקַּ֨ח מָנ֜וֹחַ אֶת גְּדִ֤י הָעִזִּים֙ וְאֶת הַמִּנְחָ֔ה וַיַּ֥עַל עַל הַצּ֖וּר לַֽיהוָ֑ה וּמַפְלִ֣א לַעֲשׂ֔וֹת וּמָנ֥וֹחַ וְאִשְׁתּ֖וֹ רֹאִֽים

verses.restored: When flame went up from altar toward heavens, messenger of YHWH went up in flame of altar. Manoah and his wife were watching, and they fell upon their faces to ground.

familiar.text: For it came to pass, when the flame went up toward heaven from off the altar, that the angel of the LORD ascended in the flame of the altar. And Manoah and his wife looked on it, and fell on their faces to the ground.

modern.text: When the flame went up from the altar to the sky, the angel of the LORD ascended in the flame. When Manoah and his wife saw this, they fell facedown to the ground.

original.text: וַיְהִי֩ בַעֲל֨וֹת הַלַּ֜הַב מֵעַ֤ל הַמִּזְבֵּ֨חַ֙ הַשָּׁמַ֔יְמָה וַיַּ֥עַל מַלְאַךְ יְהוָ֖ה בְּלַ֣הַב הַמִּזְבֵּ֑חַ וּמָנ֤וֹחַ וְאִשְׁתּוֹ֙ רֹאִ֔ים וַיִּפְּל֥וּ עַל פְּנֵיהֶ֖ם אָֽרְצָה

verses.restored: Messenger of YHWH did not again appear to Manoah and his wife. Then Manoah knew that he was messenger of YHWH.

familiar.text: But the angel of the LORD did no more appear to Manoah and to his wife. Then Manoah knew that he was an angel of the LORD.

modern.text: And when the angel of the LORD did not appear again to Manoah and his wife, Manoah realized that it had been the angel of the LORD.

original.text: וְלֹא יָ֤סַף עוֹד֙ מַלְאַ֣ךְ יְהוָ֔ה לְהֵרָאֹ֖ה אֶל מָנ֣וֹחַ וְאֶל אִשְׁתּ֑וֹ אָ֚ז יָדַ֣ע מָנ֔וֹחַ כִּֽי מַלְאַ֥ךְ יְהוָ֖ה הֽוּא

verses.restored: Manoah said to his wife, Dying, we shall die, because we have seen Divine.

familiar.text: And Manoah said unto his wife, We shall surely die, because we have seen God.

modern.text: “We are going to die,” he said to his wife, “for we have seen God!”

original.text: וַיֹּ֧אמֶר מָנ֛וֹחַ אֶל אִשְׁתּ֖וֹ מ֣וֹת נָמ֑וּת כִּ֥י אֱלֹהִ֖ים רָאִֽינוּ

verses.restored: His wife said to him, If YHWH desired to put us to death, he would not have accepted from our hand an ascending offering and grain offering, nor shown us all these things, nor at this time made us hear such a thing.

familiar.text: But his wife said unto him, If the LORD were pleased to kill us, he would not have received a burnt offering and a meat offering at our hands, neither would he have shewed us all these things, nor would as at this time have told us such things as these.

modern.text: But his wife replied, “If the LORD had intended to kill us, He would not have accepted the burnt offering and the grain offering from our hands, nor would He have shown us all these things or spoken to us this way.”

original.text: וַתֹּ֧אמֶר ל֣וֹ אִשְׁתּ֗וֹ לוּ֩ חָפֵ֨ץ יְהוָ֤ה לַהֲמִיתֵ֨נוּ֙ לֹֽא לָקַ֤ח מִיָּדֵ֨נוּ֙ עֹלָ֣ה וּמִנְחָ֔ה וְלֹ֥א הֶרְאָ֖נוּ אֶת כָּל אֵ֑לֶּה וְכָעֵ֕ת לֹ֥א הִשְׁמִיעָ֖נוּ כָּזֹֽאת

verses.restored: The woman bore a son and called his name Samson. The boy grew, and YHWH blessed him.

familiar.text: And the woman bare a son, and called his name Samson: and the child grew, and the LORD blessed him.

modern.text: So the woman gave birth to a son and named him Samson. The boy grew, and the LORD blessed him.

original.text: וַתֵּ֤לֶד הָֽאִשָּׁה֙ בֵּ֔ן וַתִּקְרָ֥א אֶת שְׁמ֖וֹ שִׁמְשׁ֑וֹן וַיִּגְדַּ֣ל הַנַּ֔עַר וַֽיְבָרְכֵ֖הוּ יְהוָֽה

verses.restored: Spirit of YHWH began to stir/impel him in Camp of Dan, between Zorah and Eshtaol.

familiar.text: And the Spirit of the LORD began to move him at times in the camp of Dan between Zorah and Eshtaol.

modern.text: And the Spirit of the LORD began to stir him at Mahaneh-dan, between Zorah and Eshtaol.

original.text: וַתָּ֨חֶל֙ ר֣וּחַ יְהוָ֔ה לְפַעֲמ֖וֹ בְּמַחֲנֵה דָ֑ן בֵּ֥ין צָרְעָ֖ה וּבֵ֥ין אֶשְׁתָּאֹֽל

translation_notes: The woman is unnamed, but she is the first recipient of the revelation, receives it twice, accurately transmits it, names the child, and offers the chapter's soundest theological reasoning.
Infertility is a bodily circumstance in the story, not a curse, punishment, shame, lack of femininity, or sign of inferior faith. The woman's value precedes pregnancy.

The dietary and hair instructions belong to this particular Nazirite birth narrative. They may not be generalized into control of pregnant people, reproductive coercion, purity policing, or denial of medical care.
Samson is consecrated before birth without personally choosing the vow. The narrative later exposes the tension between inherited calling, bodily sign, agency, and family expectation.
He will begin to save Israel; the wording anticipates incomplete deliverance rather than a flawless hero.
Manoah asks for instruction, but the messenger repeatedly directs attention back to what was already said to the woman.
Peli in verse 18 is related to wonder and may mean wondrous or beyond understanding; it need not be reduced to merely secret.
Verse 19 has an uncertain subject in 'doing wondrously' and should remain open in later audit.
Manoah fears death after the revelation; his wife reasons from accepted offering, disclosed promise, and Divine intention. Her logic corrects fear without diminishing awe.
YHWH's blessing and Spirit stirring do not certify every later act of Samson as ethical or divinely commanded.
safety_note: Do not shame infertility, childlessness, pregnancy choices, disabled bodies, or people unable or unwilling to reproduce. Do not turn the woman's temporary ritual instructions into universal control over another person's body. Center her revelation, intelligence, authority, and theological clarity; do not erase her because the text does not preserve her name.
